pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: At passport control, the officer usually asks why you are visiting.
items.why: Questions like “What’s the purpose of your visit?” are very common.

items.s: You should give long, funny answers to the officer.
items.why: Short, clear and honest answers are best.

items.s: Many visitors need a visa or a special permission to enter the USA.
items.why: It depends on the country, so check the rules before you travel.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: At passport control, the officer usually asks why you are visiting. → Verdadeiro (Questions like “What’s the purpose of your visit?” are very common.)
You should give long, funny answers to the officer. → Falso (Short, clear and honest answers are best.)
Many visitors need a visa or a special permission to enter the USA. → Verdadeiro (It depends on the country, so check the rules before you travel.)

pages.title: Lia at passport control · 1/3
paragraphs: Lia lands in **Atlanta** after a long flight. She is tired, but she is happy. This is her first trip to the USA. She follows the signs to passport control.

The line is long. Lia waits. She holds her passport and thinks about the cat movie “The Aristocats.” In the film, the cats live in Paris. “Where do I live?” she thinks. “In São Paulo. And now I am in Atlanta.” She smiles.

pages.focus: o som do w em will, week, welcome
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O w inglês é um som de lábios arredondados, como um “u” rápido. Brasileiros costumam trocá-lo por v e dizem “veeks” em vez de “weeks”, o que muda a palavra.
pages.how: Arredonde os lábios como para dizer “u”, sem encostar os dentes no lábio de baixo, e abra para a vogal seguinte. Em “week”, soa “uíik”.
pages.tip: Compare “very” (dentes no lábio) com “wary” (lábios redondos) no espelho.
